report.source_text: In preparation for planned endovascular coiling, catheter angiography of the proper hepatic artery was conducted on HOD 6. This demonstrated a lack of opacification of the aneurysm sac (figure 5A,B) suggestive of thrombosis. There was significant narrowing of mid and proximal portion of the proper hepatic artery, possibly due to compression from the adjacent thrombosed aneurysm, similar to that seen on the previous CT. To further evaluate the vascular supply to this lesion, portal venous angiography was performed on HOD 7 (figure 5C). This showed no appreciable communication between the vascular lesion and the portal vein. On HOD 7, drainage catheters were placed under ultrasound guidance in the two right hepatic liver abscesses. The third abscess was in an anatomical position unamenable to drainage.

Percutaneous drains were removed due to minimal drainage, and the patient was discharged in good condition on HOD 23 with outpatient intravenous ampicillin until the resolution of undrained liver abscess on imaging. The patient remained in good condition without abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 50s with no prior medical history presented to the emergency department with 5 days of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, yellow emesis, and one episode of hematemesis. She was afebrile (36.7°C) with leukocytosis (15.0×10^9/L, 78% neutrophils) and incidental HbA1C elevation (14.2%). CT imaging of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with liver multiphase protocol revealed three peripherally enhancing cystic lesions in hepatic segments VI (5.4×7.0×4.4 cm), VII (5.1×5.8×4.2 cm), and VIII (4.3×3.8×4.0 cm) consistent with liver abscesses, and a 3.2 cm arterially enhancing vascular lesion in the porta hepatis concerning for hepatic artery aneurysm. Empiric antibiotics (ceftriaxone 2 g every 24 hours and metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours) were initiated after blood cultures. On hospital day 6, catheter angiography of the proper hepatic artery demonstrated thrombosis of the aneurysm sac with significant narrowing of the mid and proximal proper hepatic artery. On hospital day 7, ultrasound-guided drainage catheters were placed in the two right hepatic abscesses; the third abscess was in an anatomically inaccessible location. On hospital day 12, L. monocytogenes was cultured from hepatic abscess samples. Abscesses decreased in size on repeat CT imaging on hospital days 13 and 20, and the hepatic artery aneurysm remained thrombosed. Percutaneous drains were removed due to minimal drainage. The patient was discharged on hospital day 23 in good condition on intravenous ampicillin for continued treatment of the undrained abscess. At 5 weeks of treatment, repeat CT demonstrated ongoing improvement in abscess size, and the patient was switched to oral amoxicillin. She remained in good condition without abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting.
